items.title: Disney Cuts More Than 100 Jobs In Theme Park Division
items.summary: CEO Josh D’Amaro has said he is highly focused on reducing costs at the media giant.

items.title: Alaska Airlines to Lay Off 200 Employees as It Forecasts a Loss in 2026
items.summary: Higher fuel costs have eaten into Alaska’s profits and now the carrier says it will cut 200 back office roles to help with cost control.

items.title: Hyatt in Trademark Clash With Hilton Over ‘Select’ in Hotel Brand Names
items.summary: When hotel giants keep stacking sub-brands and “brands of brands,” they eventually run out of words. Expect more naming collisions as the industry’s label factory keeps humming.

items.title: Visit Norway Turns Trump’s Insult Into Its Most-Viewed Page
items.summary: A quick tweak to a five-year-old web page has brought in tens of thousands of views to Visit Norway’s website.

items.title: Dubai Holiday-Home Operator Silkhaus Shuts Down, Citing U.S.-Iran War
items.summary: With several airlines staying out of Dubai into 2027 and forward bookings well below last year, this winter’s peak season is unlikely to rescue smaller holiday-home operators following the March and April disruption. More exits are likely.

items.title: Gravity Haus Wants to Make Mountain Life a Membership
items.summary: Gravity Haus combines hotel rooms, workspaces, and gyms to help people fit more outdoor time around work and family. Its growth depends on securing and adapting properties in competitive mountain markets, and persuading customers to pay for a new kind of membership.

items.title: Which Airlines Are Still Skipping Dubai This Winter
items.summary: Dubai’s airport is busy, but the long-haul airlines that fill its luxury hotels are mostly staying out until spring. Hotels organizing around a European winter rebound need to plan for a later one.

items.title: When Sustainability and Hospitality Performance Go Hand in Hand
items.summary: Sustainability is increasingly tied to hotel performance, from operating costs and asset value to guest experience and talent. Accor’s Coline Pont explains how the company’s new Hosting Change strategy aims to turn those connections into measurable value.
